title.rhyme: Chapter 5: At Cao's forg'd decree, lords arise to fight; Three heroes break the pass, 'gainst Lü Bu's might.
title.prose: Chapter 5: Sending forth a forged decree, the lords of every march answer Lord Cao; breaking the pass forces, three heroes battle Lü Bu.
title.original: 第五回：發矯詔諸鎮應曹公，破關兵三英戰呂布

paragraphs.original: 卻說陳宮正欲下手殺曹操，忽轉念曰：「我為國家跟他到此，殺之不義。不若棄而他往。」插劍上馬，不等天明，自投東郡去了。操覺，不見陳宮，尋思：「此人見我說了這兩句，疑我不仁，棄我而去；吾當急行，不可久留。」遂連夜到陳留，尋見父親，備說前事；欲散家資，招募義兵。父言：「資少恐不成事。此間有孝廉衛弘，疏財仗義，其家巨富；若得相助，事可圖矣。」
paragraphs.prose: Now to tell of Chen Gong, who was just about to strike Cao Cao when suddenly a thought turned in his mind: 'I followed him this far for the sake of the country — to slay him is unrighteous. Better to leave him and go elsewhere.' He sheathed his sword, mounted his horse, and without waiting for daybreak, set off alone for Dong Commandery. Cao woke, did not see Chen Gong, and pondered, 'This man, hearing those two words I spoke, suspected me of inhumanity, and abandoned me. I must hasten on; I cannot linger long.' That very night he travelled to Chenliu, found his father, and told him in full all that had passed; he wished to spend the family resources to recruit righteous troops. His father said, 'The resources are too few — I fear the matter will not succeed. Here lives a Xiaolian by name Wei Hong, generous with his wealth and steadfast in righteousness; his family is greatly rich. If you can get his help, the matter may be planned.'
paragraphs.rhyme:
Now [Chen Gong](char-chen-gong), just about [Cao Cao](char-cao-cao) to slay,
But stay'd his hand, and turn'd his mind away:
'For country's sake I follow'd to this place;
To slay him now would be unjust and base.
Better to leave!' He sheath'd his blade, and went,
Ere break of day, to Dong Comm'ndery bent.
[Cao](char-cao-cao) woke; [Gong](char-chen-gong) gone. He thought with sober mind:
'My words have made him doubt my heart be kind,
And so departs. I must in haste be gone;
Nor here may linger more — be off, anon!'
That night to [Chenliu](loc-chenliu) sped, his sire to greet,
Recounted all the past, the tale complete.
He'd spend his fam'ly wealth, recruit a band
Of righteous troops, to overthrow [Zhuo](char-dong-zhuo)'s hand.
'The wealth is small,' the father said, 'I fear
The deed may fail. But [Wei Hong](char-wei-hong) lives here near,
A Xiaolian, generous and just in mind;
His house is rich — with him, success thou'lt find.'

paragraphs.original: 操置酒張筵，拜請衛弘到家，告曰：「今漢室無主，董卓專權，欺君害民，天下切齒。操欲力扶社稷，恨力不足。公乃忠義之士，敢求相助。」衛弘曰：「吾有是心久矣，恨未遇英雄耳。既孟德有大志，願將家資相助。」操大喜；於是先發矯詔，馳報各道，然後招集義兵，豎起招兵白旗一面，上書「忠義」二字。不數日間，應募之士，如雨駢集。
paragraphs.prose: Cao set out wine, spread a banquet, and respectfully invited Wei Hong to his house, telling him, 'Now the Han house is without a master; Dong Zhuo wields all power, deceives the sovereign and harms the people; the realm grinds its teeth. I would strenuously prop up the altars of state, but my strength is too small. You, sir, are a man of loyalty and righteousness; I dare to seek your help.' Wei Hong said, 'I have had this heart for long, but lamented only that I had not met a hero. Since Mengde has great ambition, I am willing to give my family resources to help.' Cao was greatly pleased; he then first sent forged decrees galloping to all districts, then gathered righteous troops, and raised a white banner of recruitment, with the two characters "Loyal and Righteous" written upon it. Within a few days, those who answered the call gathered like rain.
paragraphs.rhyme:
[Cao Cao](char-cao-cao) spread wine, [Wei Hong](char-wei-hong) he bid attend,
And gave his suit, and pray'd his help to lend:
'The Han is masterless; [Dong Zhuo](char-dong-zhuo) alone
Wields all the pow'r, usurps the very throne,
Deceives the king, oppresses every soul;
All grind their teeth at his foul control.
I'd prop the state, but lack the strength to stand;
Thou righteous lord, I beg thy helping hand.'
Wei answer'd: 'Long this aim I've held in heart,
But found no hero to take equal part.
Since thou hath such will, my household store
Of wealth I'll lend, on thee my hopes I pour.'
[Cao](char-cao-cao) joyful, first dispatch'd through every land
Forg'd decrees in haste; then gather'd to his band
The righteous troops. He rais'd a banner plain,
Inscrib'd 'Loyal-Righteous'; came men thick as rain.

paragraphs.original: 一日，有一個陽平衛國人，姓樂，名進，字文謙，來投曹操。又有一個山陽鉅鹿人，姓李，名典，字曼成，也來投曹操。操皆留為帳前吏。又有沛國譙人，夏侯惇，字元讓，乃夏侯嬰之後；自小習鎗棒；年十四從師學武，有人辱罵其師，惇殺之，逃於外方；聞知曹操起兵，與其族弟夏侯淵兩個，各引壯士千人來會。此二人本操之弟兄：操父曹嵩原是夏侯氏之子，過房與曹家，因此是同族。
paragraphs.prose: One day, a man of the Wei kingdom in Yangping, surnamed Yue, named Jin, courtesy name Wenqian, came to join Cao Cao. There came also a man of Julu in Shanyang, surnamed Li, named Dian, courtesy name Mancheng, who likewise came to join Cao Cao. Cao kept them both as officers before his tent. There came too a man of Qiao in the kingdom of Pei, Xiahou Dun, courtesy name Yuanrang, a descendant of Xiahou Ying. From his youth he had practised spear and staff; at fourteen he had followed a master to learn the martial arts. When someone reviled his master, Dun killed him and fled abroad. Hearing that Cao Cao was raising troops, he came together with his clansman Xiahou Yuan, the two each leading a thousand stout men, to join him. These two were in fact Cao's own kin: for Cao's father Cao Song was originally a son of the Xiahou clan, who had been adopted into the Cao family; and so they were of the same lineage.
paragraphs.rhyme:
One day, from Wei in Yangping, [Yue Jin](char-yue-jin) came;
To join [Cao Cao](char-cao-cao)'s ranks, he gave his name.
And from Shanyang's Julu, [Li Dian](char-li-dian) came too,
His service unto [Cao Cao](char-cao-cao)'s host he drew.
[Cao](char-cao-cao) kept them as officers near to hand.
Then [Xiahou Dun](char-xiahou-dun), of Qiao in Pei, took stand,
Of Xiahou Ying descended. Young in age,
He trained with spear and staff beneath a sage;
When one defam'd that sage, in youthful rage,
He slew the man, and fled to lands afar.
Hearing that [Cao](char-cao-cao) had rais'd the righteous war,
Came he with clansman [Xiahou Yuan](char-xiahou-yuan) at hand,
Each leading thousand stout, a well-arm'd band.
These two were [Cao](char-cao-cao)'s own kin: for Cao Song's birth
Was Xiahou; by adoption made to Cao's hearth.

paragraphs.original: 不數日，曹氏兄弟曹仁，曹洪，各引兵千餘來助。曹仁字子孝，曹洪字子廉；二人兵馬嫺熟，武藝精通。操大喜，於村中調諫軍馬。衛弘盡出家財，置辦衣甲旗旛。四方送糧者，不計其數。
paragraphs.prose: Within a few days, the Cao brothers Cao Ren and Cao Hong each led more than a thousand troops to come to Cao's aid. Cao Ren, courtesy name Zixiao; Cao Hong, courtesy name Zilian — both were practised in horsemanship and skilled in martial arts. Cao was greatly pleased, and drilled the soldiers and horses in the village. Wei Hong gave forth all his family's wealth, and provided clothing, armour, banners, and pennons. From all directions, those who sent in provisions were past counting.
paragraphs.rhyme:
Few days had pass'd; two kinsmen of his line,
[Cao Ren](char-cao-ren) and [Cao Hong](char-cao-hong) came, with troops to join.
Each brought a thousand troops, well-used to rein,
And skilled in arms upon the battle plain.
[Cao](char-cao-cao) greatly pleas'd; he drill'd them in his town.
[Wei Hong](char-wei-hong) gave out his wealth — for shield and gown,
For banners, pennons. From the regions round,
Came in provisions, past all reck'ning's bound.

paragraphs.original: 時袁紹得操矯詔，乃聚麾下文武，引兵三萬，離渤海來與曹操會盟。操作檄文以達諸郡。檄文曰：操等謹以大義布告天下：董卓欺天罔地，滅國弒君；穢亂宮禁，殘害生靈；狼戾不仁，罪惡充積！今奉天子密詔，大集義兵，誓欲掃清華夏，剿戮群凶。望興義師，共洩公憤；扶持王室，拯救黎民。檄文到日，可速奉行！
paragraphs.prose: At that time Yuan Shao received Cao's forged decree, and so gathered his civil and military followers, and leading thirty thousand troops departed from Bohai to come and ally with Cao Cao. Cao composed a proclamation to send to all commanderies. The proclamation said, 'Cao and his fellows, with great righteousness, proclaim to the realm: Dong Zhuo deceives Heaven and deceives Earth, has ruined the state and slain the sovereign; he defiles the palace and harms the living; wolfish and vicious, without humanity, his crimes are heaped up. Now, bearing the Son of Heaven's secret edict, we have gathered a great host of righteous troops, and have sworn to sweep clean the central realm and exterminate the wicked horde. We pray you raise righteous armies, share with us the public indignation, sustain the royal house, and rescue the people. The day this proclamation arrives, act swiftly!'
paragraphs.rhyme:
[Yuan Shao](char-yuan-shao) receiv'd [Cao](char-cao-cao)'s forg'd decree, and made
His civil and his martial men array'd:
Three myriad strong, from [Bohai](loc-bohai)'s gates he led
His host, with [Cao](char-cao-cao) in solemn league were spread.
[Cao](char-cao-cao) sent writs to every commandery around,
Whose proclamation thus was made to sound:
'By righteous cause, we now to all declare
Throughout the realm, that justice be laid bare:
[Dong Zhuo](char-dong-zhuo) hath flouted heav'n, deceiv'd the earth,
Brought down the state, and slain the throne by birth.
Defil'd the palace, harm'd the living soul;
Wolf-hearted, cruel, his crimes o'erfill the scroll.
Now, by the Son of Heaven's secret seal,
We've gather'd righteous troops, the realm to heal,
To cleanse the central lands, the wicked slay,
And free the state from this oppressive day.
Pray raise the righteous host; with us combine
To vent the public wrath, to prop the line
Of royal house; the people raise from woe.
The day this writ arrives — make haste, and go!'

paragraphs.original: 操發檄文去後，各鎮諸侯，皆起兵相應：第一鎮，後將軍南陽太守袁術。第二鎮，冀州刺史韓馥。第三州鎮，豫州刺史孔。第四鎮，兗州刺史劉岱。第五鎮，河內郡太守王匡。第六鎮，陳留太守張邈。第七鎮，東郡太守喬瑁。第八鎮，山陽太守劉遺。第九鎮，濟北相鮑信。第十鎮，北海太守孔融。第十一鎮，廣陵太守張超。第十二鎮，徐州刺史陶謙。第十三鎮，西涼太守馬騰。第十四鎮，北平太守公孫瓚。第十五鎮，上黨太守張楊。第十六鎮，烏程侯長沙太守孫堅。第十七鎮，祁鄉侯渤海太守袁紹。諸路軍馬，少不等，一有三萬者，有一二萬者一，各領文官武將，投洛陽來。
paragraphs.prose: After Cao sent out the proclamation, the lords of every march raised troops in answer. The first march: Rear General, Grand Administrator of Nanyang, Yuan Shu. The second march: Inspector of Jizhou, Han Fu. The third march: Inspector of Yu Province, Kong Zhou. The fourth march: Inspector of Yan Province, Liu Dai. The fifth march: Grand Administrator of Henei Commandery, Wang Kuang. The sixth march: Grand Administrator of Chenliu, Zhang Miao. The seventh march: Grand Administrator of Dong Commandery, Qiao Mao. The eighth march: Grand Administrator of Shanyang, Liu Yi. The ninth march: Chancellor of Jibei, Bao Xin. The tenth march: Grand Administrator of Beihai, Kong Rong. The eleventh march: Grand Administrator of Guangling, Zhang Chao. The twelfth march: Inspector of Xuzhou, Tao Qian. The thirteenth march: Grand Administrator of Xiliang, Ma Teng. The fourteenth march: Grand Administrator of Beiping, Gongsun Zan. The fifteenth march: Grand Administrator of Shangdang, Zhang Yang. The sixteenth march: Marquis of Wucheng, Grand Administrator of Changsha, Sun Jian. The seventeenth march: Marquis of Qixiang, Grand Administrator of Bohai, Yuan Shao. The various armies were not equal in number — some had thirty thousand, some one or two ten-thousand — and each, leading their civil officers and military generals, made for Luoyang.

paragraphs.original: 且說北平太守公孫瓚，統領精兵一萬五千，路經德州平原縣。正行之間，遙見桑樹叢中，一面黃旗，數騎來迎。瓚視之，乃劉玄德也。瓚問曰：「賢弟何故在此？」玄德曰：「舊日蒙兄保備為平原縣令，今聞大軍過此，特來奉候，就請兄長入城歇馬。」瓚指關、張而問曰：「此何人也？」玄德曰：「此關羽，張飛，備結義兄弟也。」瓚曰：「乃同破黃巾者乎？」玄德曰：「皆此二人之力。」瓚曰：「今居何職？」玄德答曰：「關羽為馬弓手，張飛為步弓手。」瓚歎曰：「如此可謂埋沒英雄！今董卓作亂，天下諸侯，共往誅之。賢弟可棄此卑官，一同討賊，力扶漢室，若何？」玄德曰：「願往。」張飛曰：「當時若容我殺了此賊，免有今日之事。」雲長曰：「事已至此，即當收拾前去。」
paragraphs.prose: Now to tell of the Grand Administrator of Beiping, Gongsun Zan, who, at the head of fifteen thousand picked troops, was passing through Pingyuan County in Dezhou. As he marched, he saw afar within a thicket of mulberry trees a yellow flag, and several riders coming to meet him. Zan looked, and it was Liu Xuande. Zan asked, 'Worthy brother, why are you here?' Xuande said, 'In days past, by your grace, brother, I was made County Magistrate of Pingyuan; now hearing that the great army was passing here, I came especially to await you, and I beg you, elder brother, to come into the city to rest the horses.' Zan, pointing at Guan and Zhang, asked, 'Who are these?' Xuande said, 'These are Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, my sworn brothers.' Zan said, 'Are these those who broke the Yellow Turbans with you?' Xuande said, 'All by these two men's strength.' Zan said, 'What office do they now hold?' Xuande replied, 'Guan Yu serves as a mounted archer, Zhang Fei as a foot archer.' Zan sighed and said, 'This is to bury heroes! Now Dong Zhuo causes disorder, and the lords of the realm together go to execute him. Worthy brother, abandon this lowly post and join us in chastising the traitor, to uphold the Han house — what say you?' Xuande said, 'I am willing to go.' Zhang Fei said, 'If at that earlier time you had only let me kill that traitor, this day's affair would have been spared us.' Yunchang said, 'Things being come to this, let us at once make ready and go forth.'
paragraphs.rhyme:
[Gongsun Zan](char-gongsun-zan) of Beiping march'd, his banners 'long
With fifteen thousand picked men in his throng;
Through Dezhou pass'd, by Pingyuan's quiet way.
A yellow flag in mulberries that lay,
And riders forth to meet. [Zan](char-gongsun-zan) look'd, and knew —
'Twas [Liu Bei](char-liu-bei): 'Worthy brother, why come you?'
Said [Bei](char-liu-bei): 'Through thy old grace, this post is mine
Of Pingyuan's Magistrate; thy army's line
I heard pass by, and came to greet thee here;
Pray come into the city, rest thy gear.'
[Zan](char-gongsun-zan) ask'd: 'Who are these two who stand by thee?'
Said [Bei](char-liu-bei): 'My sworn brothers, [Guan Yu](char-guan-yu), [Zhang Fei](char-zhang-fei).'
[Zan](char-gongsun-zan): 'Are these who broke the Yellow Turbans bold?'
'All by their strength.' [Zan](char-gongsun-zan): 'What office hold
They now?' Said [Bei](char-liu-bei): '[Guan Yu](char-guan-yu) is mounted-bow,
[Zhang Fei](char-zhang-fei) is foot-archer.' [Zan](char-gongsun-zan) sigh'd: 'Below
What heroes thus are buried! Now in pow'r,
[Dong Zhuo](char-dong-zhuo) brings chaos to the realm this hour.
The lords are gather'd all the foe to slay;
Abandon thou this lowly post today,
Join us in chastising of the bane,
With all thy strength, prop up the Han again.'
Said [Bei](char-liu-bei): 'I'm willing.' [Zhang Fei](char-zhang-fei) cried in pain:
'Had I but slain him then, this hour were vain.'
[Guan Yu](char-guan-yu): 'Things stand thus now; prepare to ride,
Make ready forth, and let us journey wide.'

paragraphs.original: 玄德、關、張引數騎跟公孫瓚來。曹操接著。眾諸侯亦陸續皆至，各自安營下寨，連接二百餘里。操乃宰牛殺馬，大會諸侯，商議進兵之策。太守王匡曰：「今奉大義，必立盟主；眾聽約束，然後進兵。」操曰：「袁本初四世三公，門多故吏，漢朝名相之裔，可為盟主。」紹再三推辭。眾皆曰：「非本初不可。」紹方應允。次日築臺三層，遍列五方旗幟，上建白旄黃鉞，兵符將印，請紹登壇。紹整衣佩劍，慨然而上，焚香再拜。其盟曰：漢室不幸，皇綱失統。賊臣董卓，乘釁縱害，禍加至尊，虐流百姓。紹等懼社稷淪喪，糾合義兵，並赴國難。凡我同盟，齊心戮力，以致臣節，必無二志。有渝此盟，俾墜其命，無克遺育。皇天后土，祖宗明靈，實皆鑒之！
paragraphs.prose: Xuande, Guan, and Zhang led some riders and followed Gongsun Zan. Cao Cao welcomed them. The other lords also arrived in succession, and each set up his own camp; the connected camps stretched more than two hundred li. Cao slaughtered cattle and horses, and held a great gathering of the lords to discuss the strategy of advancing. Grand Administrator Wang Kuang said, 'Now bearing great righteousness, we must establish a chief of the alliance; let all heed his commands, and then we shall advance.' Cao said, 'Yuan Benchu — of four generations of Three Dukes, with many former officials at his gate, descendant of a famed chancellor of the Han — he may serve as alliance chief.' Shao thrice declined. All said, 'There is none but Benchu.' Shao then assented. The next day they built an altar of three tiers, arrayed banners of the five directions, set up the white-yak-tail standard and the yellow battle-axe, the military commission and the general's seal, and invited Shao to ascend the altar. Shao straightened his robes, girded his sword, and ascended in solemn dignity, burned incense and bowed twice. The oath ran: 'The Han house is unfortunate, the imperial line has lost its succession. The traitor minister Dong Zhuo, taking advantage of the breach, lets his harm range unchecked, brings calamity upon the most honoured, and lets cruelty flow upon the people. Shao and his fellows, fearing the altars of state will fall, have gathered righteous troops and rushed all together to the country's distress. We, all who are bound in this oath, shall with one heart exert our strength to fulfil the duty of ministers, and have no second mind. Whoever shall break this oath, let him lose his life and leave no posterity. August Heaven, Sovereign Earth, the bright spirits of the ancestors — all bear witness!'
paragraphs.rhyme:
With [Gongsun Zan](char-gongsun-zan) came [Liu Bei](char-liu-bei) and his pair;
[Cao Cao](char-cao-cao) welcom'd them all, in solemn air.
The other lords by stages came, in train,
Each pitching camp, that link'd along the plain
Two hundred li of conjoin'd canvas-wave.
[Cao](char-cao-cao) slaughter'd beeves and horses, lavish gave
A great feast to all lords, that they discuss
The march. [Wang Kuang](char-wang-kuang): 'Just cause summons us;
We needs must set a chief whom all approve;
Let all submit, and forward then to move.'
[Cao](char-cao-cao) said: '[Benchu](char-yuan-shao), of four-fold ducal line,
Of famous Han chancellor — fit to shine
As alliance-chief.' [Shao](char-yuan-shao) thrice declin'd; the crowd
Cried, 'None but he!' with one consent aloud.
[Shao](char-yuan-shao) then assent. Next day, three-tier'd they made
An altar; five-fold compass-banners stay'd;
White yak-tail standard, yellow axe of state,
The general's seal — bid [Shao](char-yuan-shao) ascend the gate.
[Shao](char-yuan-shao) straighten'd robes, gird sword, with steady tread
Ascended; burn'd incense, bow'd; thus he said:
'The Han is luckless; rule hath lost its line.
The traitor [Dong Zhuo](char-dong-zhuo) seiz'd the breach malign,
Wreaks harm upon the throne, oppresses men.
We, fearing fall of state, have rais'd amain
A righteous host. All in this oath one mind,
Steadfast in duty; no two thoughts to find.
Whoso betrays — let him lose life, and ne'er
Bear sons to follow him. — Heaven, Earth, and air,
All ancestral spirits, glorious and bright,
We pray you witness this our solemn rite!'

paragraphs.original: 讀畢，歃血。眾因其辭氣慷慨，皆涕泗橫流。歃血已罷，下壇。眾扶紹升帳而坐，兩行依爵位年齒分列坐定。操行酒數巡，言曰：「今日既立盟主，各聽調遣，同扶國家，勿以強弱計較。」袁紹曰：「紹雖不才，既承公等推為盟主，有功必賞，有罪必罰。國有常刑，軍有紀律；各宜遵守，勿得違犯。」眾皆曰：「惟命是聽。」紹曰：「吾弟袁術總督糧草，應付諸營，無使有缺。更須一人為先鋒，直抵汜水關挑戰。餘各據險要，以為接應。」長沙太守孫堅出曰：「堅願為前部。」紹曰：「文臺勇烈，可當此任。」堅遂引本部人馬殺奔汜水關來。守關將士，差流星馬往洛陽丞相府告急。董卓自專大權之後，每日飲宴。李儒接得告急文書，逕來稟卓。卓大驚，急聚眾將商議。溫侯呂布挺身出曰：「父親勿慮：關外諸侯，布視之如草芥。願提虎狼之師，盡斬其首，懸於都門。」卓大喜曰：「吾有奉先，高枕無憂矣！」言未絕，呂布背後一人高聲出曰：「『割雞焉用牛刀？』不勞溫侯親往。吾斬眾諸侯首級，如探囊取物耳。」卓視之，其人身長九尺，虎體狼腰，豹頭猿臂：關西人也；姓華，名雄。卓聞言大喜，加為驍騎校尉，撥馬步軍五萬，同李肅，胡軫，趙岑星夜赴關迎敵。眾諸侯內有濟北相鮑信，尋思孫堅既為前部，怕他奪了頭功，暗撥其弟鮑忠，先將馬步軍三千，逕抄小路，直到關下搦戰。華雄引鐵騎五百，飛下關來，大喝：「賊將休走！」鮑忠急待退，被華雄手起刀落，斬於馬下，生擒將校極多。華雄遣人將鮑忠首級來相府報捷，卓加雄為都督。
paragraphs.prose: When the reading was done, they smeared blood. All, moved by the solemn earnestness of his words, wept streams of tears. The smearing of blood being done, they descended the altar. They helped Shao up to the tent, where he sat; the company seated themselves in two rows by rank and age. After the wine had gone several rounds, Cao said, 'Today, since the alliance chief has been established, let all heed his commands and uphold the country together — let there be no calculations of strong and weak.' Yuan Shao said, 'Shao, though without merit, having been pushed forward by you all to be alliance chief, will surely reward those of merit and punish those of crime. The state has its constant law; the army has its discipline. All ought to obey them, and not transgress.' All said, 'We obey only your command.' Shao said, 'My brother Yuan Shu shall oversee the provisions and supply all the camps, that none may lack. Further, one man is needed as vanguard, to advance straight to Sishui Pass and challenge battle. The rest of you, hold each your strong points, ready to support him.' The Grand Administrator of Changsha, Sun Jian, stepped forth and said, 'I am willing to serve as vanguard.' Shao said, 'Wentai is brave and fierce — he is fit for this task.' Jian then led his own troops to charge upon Sishui Pass. The officers and soldiers guarding the pass dispatched express messengers to the Chancellor's mansion at Luoyang to report the urgency. Dong Zhuo, since he had taken sole command of the great power, daily set forth wine and feasting. Li Ru, receiving the urgent dispatch, came at once to inform Zhuo. Zhuo was greatly alarmed, and at once gathered his generals to take counsel. Marquis Wen Lü Bu thrust himself forth and said, 'Father, do not be troubled. The lords beyond the pass — I look upon them as straw. Let me lead a tiger-and-wolf army, and I shall cut off all their heads, to be hung at the gates of the capital.' Zhuo, greatly pleased, said, 'With Fengxian by me, I lay my head upon a high pillow without care!' The words were not yet finished when, from behind Lü Bu, a man cried aloud, '"Why use a beef-cleaver to slaughter a chicken?" There is no need for the Marquis Wen to go in person. I will cut off the heads of all the lords as easily as a man takes things from a bag!' Zhuo looked: the man was nine chi tall, with a tiger's body and a wolf's waist, a leopard's head and an ape's arms — a man of Guanxi, surnamed Hua, named Xiong. Zhuo, hearing his words, was greatly pleased, and made him Xiaoji Cavalry Colonel, dispatched fifty thousand horse and foot, and sent him with Li Su, Hu Zhen, and Zhao Cen, to hasten through the night to the pass and meet the foe. Among the lords, Bao Xin, the Chancellor of Jibei, thinking that since Sun Jian was vanguard he might steal the first merit, secretly sent his brother Bao Zhong with three thousand horse and foot, by a small road, to charge straight to the foot of the pass and challenge. Hua Xiong led five hundred iron cavalry and flew down from the pass, shouting, 'Rebel general, halt!' Bao Zhong tried hastily to retreat; with one rise and one fall of Hua Xiong's blade, he was cut down from his horse, and many officers and soldiers were taken alive. Hua Xiong sent men with Bao Zhong's head to the Chancellor's mansion to report the victory. Zhuo promoted Xiong to Commander-in-Chief.
paragraphs.rhyme:
The reading done, they smear'd the blood, and wept,
Mov'd by [Shao](char-yuan-shao)'s solemn words, in tears unkept.
They left the altar, help'd [Shao](char-yuan-shao) up to tent,
Where, rank'd by age, in two-fold rows they bent.
[Cao](char-cao-cao) pour'd the wine and said: 'A chief now found,
Let all heed his commands, the state to bound;
Let strong and weak alike obey one hand.'
'Though small my merit, since ye give command,
Reward and punishment alike shall stand;
Law of state, discipline of camp, abide!'
All cried: 'We hear thy will!' [Shao](char-yuan-shao) thus replied:
'[Yuan Shu](char-yuan-shu), my brother, shall the grain command,
And serve all camps; let none go short of hand.
A vanguard one must be — to charge the way
'Gainst [Sishui Pass](loc-sishui-pass); the rest shall stand at bay.'
[Sun Jian](char-sun-jian) of Changsha rose: 'Vanguard be I.'
[Shao](char-yuan-shao): '[Wentai](char-sun-jian) is bold; this charge let him espy.'
[Jian](char-sun-jian) led his troops, charg'd to [Sishui Pass](loc-sishui-pass);
The pass-guards sent express to [Luoyang](loc-luoyang)'s mass,
To [Dong Zhuo](char-dong-zhuo)'s mansion. Zhuo, since pow'r supreme,
Held banquet day by day, in lavish gleam.
[Li Ru](char-li-ru) receiv'd the dispatch — in haste came;
Zhuo, startl'd, gather'd generals; counsel claim'd.
Marquis Wen [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) arose: 'No fear,
Father — those lords beyond as straw appear;
Let me lead tiger-wolves; their heads I'll hew,
And hang them at the gates for all to view.'
Zhuo cried in joy: 'With [Bu](char-lu-bu), my mind's at rest!'
But ere he ended, from behind, addrest:
'"Why use a beef-axe to cut up a hen?"
No Marquis Wen need go — I'll lead the men.
I'll lop the lords' heads, easy as a pluck
Of fruit from bag.' Zhuo saw — a man, in luck
Of stature: nine chi tall, of fierce-built frame,
Tiger-body, wolf-waist, leopard-head; the same
Was Guanxi-born — [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong) his very name.
Zhuo, hearing him, gave joy with brightest flame:
Made Xiaoji Colonel; sent forth in haste
Five myriad troops with [Li Su](char-li-su), Hu Zhen, plac'd,
And Zhao Cen, through the night, unto the pass.
Among the lords, [Bao Xin](char-bao-xin)'s thought ran amass:
'[Sun Jian](char-sun-jian) as vanguard, first shall win repute.'
He sent his brother Bao Zhong in pursuit,
With three thousand troops, to the pass.
[Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong), with five hundred iron horse, in mass,
Flew down: 'Rebel general, halt!' Bao Zhong tried
To flee; but [Xiong](char-hua-xiong)'s blade fell — and Zhong dy'd.
Many he captur'd. Bao Zhong's head he sent;
Zhuo nam'd [Xiong](char-hua-xiong) Commander-in-Chief, content.

paragraphs.original: 卻說孫堅引四將直至關前。那四將：第一個，右北平土垠人：姓程，名普，字德謀，使一條鐵脊蛇矛；第二個，姓黃，名蓋，字公覆，零陵人也，使鐵鞭：第三個，姓韓，名當，字義公，遼西令支人也，使一口大刀；第四個，姓祖，名茂，字大榮，吳郡富春人也，使雙刀。孫堅披爛銀鎧，裏赤幘，橫古錠刀，騎花鬃馬，指關上而罵曰：「助惡匹夫，何不早降！」
paragraphs.prose: Now to tell of Sun Jian, who led four generals straight to the front of the pass. The four generals were these: the first, a man of Tuyin in Right Beiping, surnamed Cheng, named Pu, courtesy name Demou, who used an iron-spined serpent-spear; the second, surnamed Huang, named Gai, courtesy name Gongfu, a man of Lingling, who used an iron whip; the third, surnamed Han, named Dang, courtesy name Yigong, a man of Lingzhi in Liaoxi, who used a great sword; the fourth, surnamed Zu, named Mao, courtesy name Darong, a man of Fuchun in Wu Commandery, who used a pair of swords. Sun Jian wore bright silver scale-armour, with a red headband, and bore his Guding sword crosswise, riding a horse with a flowered mane. Pointing up at the pass, he cursed, 'Helpers of evil, base men, why do you not surrender at once?'
paragraphs.rhyme:
[Sun Jian](char-sun-jian) led forth four men to pass-front fierce:
[Cheng Pu](char-cheng-pu) of Tuyin first came forth to pierce
With serpent-spear; then [Huang Gai](char-huang-gai) join'd the fray,
Of Lingling born, with iron whip in play.
Third was [Han Dang](char-han-dang) of Lingzhi, with great blade;
Fourth [Zu Mao](char-zu-mao) of Wu, with twin-swords display'd.
[Sun Jian](char-sun-jian) wore silver scales, red turban tied,
On flower-maned steed, his Guding sword at side.
Up at the pass he curs'd: 'Ye base of plot,
Helpers of evil — why surrender not?'

paragraphs.original: 華雄副將胡軫引兵五千出關迎戰。程普飛馬挺矛，直取胡軫。鬥不數合，程普刺中胡軫咽喉，死於馬下。堅揮軍直殺至關前，關上矢石如雨。孫堅引兵回至梁東屯住，使人於袁紹處報捷，就於袁術處催糧。或說術曰：「孫堅乃江東猛虎；若打破洛陽，殺了董卓，正是除狼而得虎也。今不與糧，彼軍必散。」術聽之，不發糧草。孫堅軍缺食，軍中自亂，細作報上關來。李肅為華雄謀曰：「今夜我引一軍從小路下關，襲孫堅寨後，將軍揮其前寨，堅可擒矣。」
paragraphs.prose: Hua Xiong's lieutenant Hu Zhen led five thousand troops out of the pass to meet him. Cheng Pu galloped his horse forth with spear levelled, and went straight at Hu Zhen. They had not fought many rounds when Cheng Pu pierced Hu Zhen through the throat, and he fell dead from his horse. Jian led his army in a charge straight up to the pass, but arrows and stones rained down from above. Sun Jian led his troops back to encamp at Liang East, and sent men to Yuan Shao to report the victory, and at the same time pressed Yuan Shu for provisions. Someone said to Shu, 'Sun Jian is the fierce tiger of Jiangdong; if he should break Luoyang and slay Dong Zhuo, that would be ridding ourselves of a wolf and gaining a tiger. If you do not give him provisions now, his army will surely scatter.' Shu listened to him, and did not dispatch the provisions. Sun Jian's army was short of food, and disorder arose within. A spy reported it up to the pass. Li Su counselled Hua Xiong, saying, 'Tonight let me lead a force down the pass by a small road, to surprise Sun Jian's rear camp; and you, General, attack his front camp. Jian can be captured.'
paragraphs.rhyme:
Hu Zhen, [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong)'s lieutenant, led along
Five thousand from the pass to meet the throng.
[Cheng Pu](char-cheng-pu) flew forth, his serpent-spear in hand;
Few rounds, Hu's throat was pierc'd; he fell to land.
[Sun Jian](char-sun-jian) charg'd up; on pass-front rain'd amain
The arrow-stones; he turn'd his troops again.
At Liang-east halt'd, [Sun Jian](char-sun-jian) sent abroad
Word of his victory to [Yuan Shao](char-yuan-shao)'s ward,
And press'd [Yuan Shu](char-yuan-shu) for grain. To Shu one said:
'[Sun Jian](char-sun-jian) is [Jiangdong](loc-jiangdong)'s fierce tiger, much to dread;
Should [Luoyang](loc-luoyang) fall, and [Dong Zhuo](char-dong-zhuo) by him slain,
'Tis trading wolf for tiger — both our bane.
Withhold the grain — his force shall self-disband.'
Shu hearken'd, and the stores stayed in his hand.
[Sun Jian](char-sun-jian)'s host grew lean; their lines began to fray;
A spy brought word up to the pass straightway.
[Li Su](char-li-su) advis'd: 'This night, by hidden way,
Down from the pass, I'll lead a force, and lay
A strike on rear-camp; thou the front pursue.
[Sun](char-sun-jian), caught between, must fall to me and you.'

paragraphs.original: 雄從之，傳令軍士飽餐，乘夜下關。是夜月白風清。到堅寨時，已是半夜，鼓譟直進。堅慌忙披掛上馬，正遇華雄。兩馬相交，鬥不數合，後面李肅軍到，令軍士放起火來。堅軍亂竄。眾將各自混戰，止有祖茂跟定孫堅，突圍而走。背後華雄追來。堅取箭，連放兩箭，皆被華雄躲過。再放第三箭時，因用力太猛，拽折了鵲畫弓，只得棄弓縱馬而奔。祖茂曰：「主公頭上赤幘射目，為賊所識認。可脫幘與某戴之。」堅就脫幘換茂盔，分兩路而走。雄軍只望赤幘者追趕，堅乃從小路得脫。祖茂被華雄追急，將赤幘挂於人家燒不盡的庭柱上，卻入樹林潛躲。
paragraphs.prose: Xiong followed his counsel, and ordered the soldiers to eat their fill, and to descend the pass under cover of night. That night the moon was bright and the wind was clear. When they reached Jian's camp, it was already midnight; with drums and shouts they pressed straight in. Jian, hastily armouring himself, mounted his horse, and met Hua Xiong. As the two horses crossed, they had not fought many rounds when Li Su's force came up behind, and ordered the soldiers to set fires. Jian's army scattered in confusion. The generals fought separately in the melee; only Zu Mao kept by Sun Jian, and broke through the encirclement to flee. Hua Xiong pursued behind. Jian took up his bow and shot two arrows in succession, both of which Hua Xiong dodged. As he was about to shoot the third arrow, the force was too great, and snapped his magpie-painted bow; he had no choice but to throw the bow away and gallop on. Zu Mao said, 'My lord's red turban upon his head is too bright a target — the rebels recognize you by it. Take it off, and let me wear it.' Jian took off his turban, exchanged it for Mao's helmet, and they parted in two directions to flee. Xiong's men only kept watching for the red turban as they pursued, and so Jian escaped by a small path. Zu Mao, hard-pressed by Hua Xiong, hung the red turban upon a half-burnt courtyard pillar of a peasant's house, and slipped into a wood to hide.
paragraphs.rhyme:
[Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong) approv'd; he bid his soldiers dine,
Then march at dusk: the night was clear and fine,
The moon shone white. They reach'd Sun's camp at last
By midnight; drums and shouts came rolling fast.
[Sun Jian](char-sun-jian), in haste array'd, leapt to his horse,
Just met [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong). Their steeds clash'd in their course.
Few rounds had pass'd; behind came [Li Su](char-li-su)'s band,
Who bade the soldiers set the fires at hand.
Sun's troops in panic fled; the captains fought
Each on his own. [Zu Mao](char-zu-mao) alone had sought
To stay by Sun, and broke the ring at last.
[Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong) pursu'd. Sun, with his bow held fast,
Sent twice his shafts — both dodg'd. The third he drew
With force too fierce; the magpie bow snapp'd through.
He cast it from him, spurr'd his horse, and fled.
[Zu Mao](char-zu-mao) call'd: 'My lord, thy turban red
Marks thee a target known; rebels are led
Thereby. Doff thou; let me wear in thy stead.'
Sun gave the turban, took Mao's helm anew;
On two roads parted; swift each rider flew.
[Xiong](char-hua-xiong)'s men, all eyes on red, pursu'd that one;
Sun by a small path slipp'd, escape was won.
[Zu Mao](char-zu-mao), hard press'd by [Xiong](char-hua-xiong) close at his back,
Hung up the turban — on a pillar black,
Half-burn'd, a peasant's courtyard post — then drew
Into the wood; in trees, he hid from view.

paragraphs.original: 華雄軍於下遙月見赤幘，四面圍定，不敢近前。用箭射之，方知是計，遂向前取了赤幘。祖茂於林後殺出，揮雙刀欲劈華雄；雄大喝一聲，將祖茂一刀砍於馬下。殺至天明，雄方引兵上關。程普，黃蓋，韓當都來尋見孫堅，再收拾軍馬屯紮。堅為折了祖茂，傷感不已，星夜遣人報知袁紹。紹大驚曰：「不想孫文臺敗於華雄之手！」便聚眾諸侯商議。眾人都到，只有公孫瓚後至，紹請入帳列坐。紹曰：「前日鮑將軍之弟不遵調遣，擅自進兵，殺身喪命，折了許多軍士。今者孫文臺又敗於華雄：挫動銳氣，為之奈何？」諸侯並皆不語。
paragraphs.prose: Hua Xiong's men, seeing the red turban afar in the moonlight, surrounded it on all sides but did not dare draw near. They shot arrows at it, and only then knew it was a ruse; they advanced and took the red turban. Zu Mao burst forth from behind the wood, brandishing his pair of swords to chop down Hua Xiong; Xiong gave a great shout, and with a single blow of his blade cut Zu Mao down from his horse. They fought till dawn, and then Xiong led his troops back up the pass. Cheng Pu, Huang Gai, and Han Dang all came and found Sun Jian, and gathered the troops once more to encamp. Jian, grieved at the loss of Zu Mao, sent men through the night to Yuan Shao to report. Shao was greatly alarmed, and said, 'I had not thought that Sun Wentai would be defeated by Hua Xiong's hand!' He at once gathered the lords for council. All came; only Gongsun Zan came late. Shao invited him into the tent and seated him. Shao said, 'The other day, General Bao's brother, not heeding the orders, presumed to advance, lost his life, and lost many of our soldiers. Now Sun Wentai too is defeated by Hua Xiong: our spirits are blunted — what is to be done?' None of the lords spoke.
paragraphs.rhyme:
[Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong)'s men below saw, in the moon,
The turban red; they circled round as soon
As they drew up, but durst not near. They shot
With arrows, knowing then 'twas but a plot;
And forward drew, and took the turban down.
[Zu Mao](char-zu-mao) sprang from wood, his twin-blades shown,
To cleave [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong); but [Xiong](char-hua-xiong), with one great cry,
Swung blade — Mao fell'd to ground, no more to fly.
They fought till dawn; [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong) withdrew to the pass.
[Cheng Pu](char-cheng-pu), [Huang Gai](char-huang-gai), [Han Dang](char-han-dang) found [Sun Jian](char-sun-jian)'s mass,
Regather'd ranks, and camp'd the wearied host.
Sun, griev'd by [Zu Mao](char-zu-mao)'s fall, by night-courier post
Sent word to [Shao](char-yuan-shao). [Shao](char-yuan-shao), startled, said:
'I had not thought [Wentai](char-sun-jian) by [Xiong](char-hua-xiong)'s blade dread
Should fall defeated!' Council straight he made;
All lords came in; but [Gongsun Zan](char-gongsun-zan) delay'd,
Came last. [Shao](char-yuan-shao) bade him sit. Then [Shao](char-yuan-shao) thus spoke:
'Days past, [Bao Xin](char-bao-xin)'s own brother heedless broke
Of all our orders, of himself advanc'd,
Lost life, and lost much host. Now too is chanc'd
That [Wentai](char-sun-jian) by [Xiong](char-hua-xiong) is fall'n. Our spirit keen
Is blunt'd. — What's our course?' Naught fell between
The lords' replies; silence held the scene.

paragraphs.original: 紹舉目遍視，見公孫瓚背後立著三人，容貌異常，都在那裏冷笑。紹問曰：「公孫太守背後何人？」瓚呼玄德出曰：「此吾自幼同舍兄弟，平原令劉備是也。」曹操曰：「莫非破黃巾劉玄德乎？」瓚曰：「然。」即令劉玄德拜見。瓚將玄德功勞，並其出身，細說一遍。紹曰：「既是漢室宗派，取坐來。」命坐。備遜謝。紹曰：「吾非敬汝名爵，吾敬汝是帝室之冑耳。」玄德乃坐於末位，關、張叉手侍立於後。
paragraphs.prose: Shao raised his eyes and looked around, and saw three men standing behind Gongsun Zan, of unusual bearing, all smiling coldly there. Shao asked, 'Who are these standing behind Grand Administrator Gongsun?' Zan called Xuande forth, saying, 'This is my schoolmate from boyhood, Liu Bei, the County Magistrate of Pingyuan.' Cao Cao said, 'Could it be Liu Xuande, who broke the Yellow Turbans?' Zan said, 'It is.' He at once bid Liu Xuande pay his respects. Zan recounted Xuande's merits, and his lineage, in full. Shao said, 'Since he is of the Han imperial line, take a seat for him.' He ordered him to sit. Bei thanked him in modest words. Shao said, 'It is not your name and rank that I honour — I honour you because you are a scion of the imperial house.' Xuande then sat in the lowest place, with Guan and Zhang standing behind him with crossed arms in attendance.
paragraphs.rhyme:
[Shao](char-yuan-shao) cast his eyes; behind [Gongsun Zan](char-gongsun-zan)'s post
Stood three of unwont mien, a smiling host
Of cold demeanour. [Shao](char-yuan-shao) ask'd: 'Behind
Thy seat, lord Gongsun, who are these I find?'
[Zan](char-gongsun-zan) call'd [Liu Bei](char-liu-bei) forth: 'A boyhood friend,
Once schoolmate sworn — [Liu Bei](char-liu-bei), whose hands attend
Pingyuan's Magistracy.' [Cao](char-cao-cao) inquir'd:
'Is this [Xuande](char-liu-bei), at whose strong hand expir'd
The Yellow Turbans' force?' [Zan](char-gongsun-zan): ''Tis he.'
He bade [Liu Bei](char-liu-bei) bow forth; and told them free
[Bei](char-liu-bei)'s merits and his lineage, full and clear.
[Shao](char-yuan-shao) said: 'Of Han's imperial line — bring near
A seat for him.' [Bei](char-liu-bei) thank'd in modest air.
[Shao](char-yuan-shao): 'Not thy name and rank do I revere;
'Tis for thy royal blood thou'rt honour'd here.'
[Bei](char-liu-bei) sat the lowest seat. [Guan Yu](char-guan-yu), [Zhang Fei](char-zhang-fei),
Behind, with arms cross'd, stood in proper stay.

paragraphs.original: 忽探子來報：「華雄引鐵騎下關，用長竿挑著孫太守赤幘，來寨前大罵搦戰。」紹曰：「誰敢去戰？」袁術背後轉出驍將俞涉曰：「小將願往。」紹喜，便著俞涉出馬。即時報來：「俞涉與華雄戰不三合，被華雄斬了。」眾大驚。太守韓馥曰：「吾有上將潘鳳，可斬華雄。」紹急令出戰。潘鳳手提大斧上馬。去不多時，飛馬來報：「潘鳳又被華雄斬了。」眾皆失色。紹曰：「可惜吾上將顏良、文醜未至！得一人在此，何懼華雄？」言未畢，階下一人大呼出曰：「小將軍願往斬華雄頭，獻於帳下！」眾視之，見其人身長九尺，髯長二尺；丹鳳眼，臥蠶眉；面如重棗，聲如巨鐘；立於帳前。紹問何人。公孫瓚曰：「此劉玄德之弟關羽也。」紹問見居何職。瓚曰：「跟隨劉玄德充馬弓手。」帳上袁術大喝曰：「汝欺吾眾諸侯無大將耶？量一弓手，安敢亂言！與我打出！」曹操急止之曰：「公路息怒：此人既出大言，必有勇略；試教出馬，如其不勝，責之未遲。」袁紹曰：「使一弓手出戰，必被華雄所笑。」操曰：「此人儀表不俗，華雄安知他是弓手？」關公曰：「如不勝，請斬某頭。」
paragraphs.prose: Suddenly a scout came in to report, 'Hua Xiong is leading iron cavalry down from the pass; on a long pole he carries Grand Administrator Sun's red turban, and is before our camp cursing and challenging.' Shao said, 'Who dares go and fight him?' From behind Yuan Shu stepped forth a stout general, Yu She, who said, 'Your humble general is willing to go.' Shao was pleased, and bid Yu She ride out. Soon there came a report, 'Yu She, fighting Hua Xiong less than three rounds, was beheaded by Hua Xiong.' All were greatly shocked. Grand Administrator Han Fu said, 'I have a superior general, Pan Feng, who can behead Hua Xiong.' Shao at once ordered him out to fight. Pan Feng, taking up his great axe, mounted his horse. Not long after, a flying horseman came in to report, 'Pan Feng has also been beheaded by Hua Xiong.' All changed colour. Shao said, 'Pity that my superior generals Yan Liang and Wen Chou are not yet here! Were one of them here, what fear should we have of Hua Xiong?' The words were not yet finished when, from below the steps, a man cried aloud, 'Your humble general is willing to go and cut off Hua Xiong's head, and present it before the tent!' All looked: the man was nine chi tall, his beard two chi long; with phoenix eyes and silkworm brows, his face like a ripe jujube, his voice like a great bell — there he stood before the tent. Shao asked who he was. Gongsun Zan said, 'This is Liu Xuande's brother, Guan Yu.' Shao asked what office he now held. Zan said, 'He follows Liu Xuande as a mounted archer.' Yuan Shu, in the upper seat, shouted angrily, 'Do you despise our lords as having no great generals? An archer dares to speak so wildly! Drive him out for me!' Cao Cao quickly stopped him, 'Gonglu, calm your wrath: this man, since he has spoken so boldly, must have valour and strategy. Try sending him forth to fight; if he should not win, it will not be too late to chastise him then.' Yuan Shao said, 'If we send out an archer, we shall surely be laughed at by Hua Xiong.' Cao said, 'This man's bearing is uncommon — how would Hua Xiong know him for an archer?' Lord Guan said, 'If I do not win, I beg you to behead me.'
paragraphs.rhyme:
A scout came in: '[Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong) leads iron horse
Down from the pass; on long pole he doth course
[Sun Jian](char-sun-jian)'s red turban high; before our wall
He curses loud, and challenges us all.'
[Shao](char-yuan-shao) ask'd: 'Who dares?' From [Yuan Shu](char-yuan-shu)'s rear, in haste,
Stepp'd Yu She, valiant: 'Let me forth be plac'd!'
[Shao](char-yuan-shao), pleas'd, bade him out to fight, and ride.
Soon came report: 'Yu She, ere three rounds tried,
By [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong)'s blade was slain.' All stood dismay'd.
Then [Han Fu](char-han-fu), Inspector, said: 'I have a blade,
Pan Feng, my superior — he may take
[Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong)'s head.' [Shao](char-yuan-shao) bade Pan Feng quickly make
The trial. Pan Feng, with great axe in his hand,
Mounted, rode out. Soon, flying o'er the land,
A horseman came: 'Pan Feng too has been slain
By [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong).' All grew pale. [Shao](char-yuan-shao) cried in pain:
'Alas — my generals [Yan Liang](char-yan-liang) and [Wen Chou](char-wen-chou)
Are yet not come. Were one of them but now
At hand, what fear had we of [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong)?' Ere
Those words were ended, from the steps came there
A voice that loudly cried: 'Your humble man
Begs to go forth, to bring — as fast as can,
[Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong)'s head, and lay it 'fore this tent!'
All look'd: nine chi he stood, magnificent;
A beard two chi; with phoenix eyes that ran
'Neath silkworm brows; his face like ripe-jujube tan,
His voice a great bell — there he stood at hand.
[Shao](char-yuan-shao) ask'd the man; [Zan](char-gongsun-zan) answer'd on demand:
'This is [Xuande](char-liu-bei)'s sworn brother — [Guan Yu](char-guan-yu) his name.'
[Shao](char-yuan-shao) ask'd what office. [Zan](char-gongsun-zan): 'A mounted bowman, claim
Of [Xuande](char-liu-bei)'s troop.' [Yuan Shu](char-yuan-shu), upper-seat'd, did frown
And thunder'd: 'Dost thou hold our lords as down
With no great generals? A bowman dares
To speak so wildly! Drive him out from there!'
[Cao](char-cao-cao) hast'ly stay'd him: '[Gonglu](char-yuan-shu), thy wrath restrain.
This man hath spoken bold — he must contain
Some valour, plan. Test him in single fight;
If he should fail, chastise him then aright.'
[Shao](char-yuan-shao): 'A bowman sent? Our lords shall all be shamed;
[Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong) will laugh to hear an archer named.'
[Cao](char-cao-cao): 'His bearing shows no common might;
How shall [Xiong](char-hua-xiong) know his rank within the fight?'
[Guan Yu](char-guan-yu) cried: 'If I fail to take his head,
Then let my own be struck from me instead.'

paragraphs.original: 操教釃熱酒一盃，與關公飲了上馬。關公曰：「酒且斟下，某去便來。」出帳提刀，飛身上馬。眾諸侯聽得關外鼓聲大振，喊聲大舉，如天摧地塌，岳撼山崩，眾皆失驚。正欲探聽，鸞鈴響處，馬到中軍，雲長提華雄之頭，擲於地上，其酒當溫。後人有詩讚之曰：威鎮乾坤第一功，轅門畫鼓響鼕鼕。雲長停盞施英勇，酒當溫時斬華雄。
paragraphs.prose: Cao ordered a cup of hot wine poured out, and gave it to Lord Guan to drink before mounting. Lord Guan said, 'Pour the wine, set it down — I will go and come right back.' He went out of the tent, took up his blade, and leapt onto his horse. The lords heard, beyond the pass, the drums roar with a great booming, and the cries rise in a great wave, as though heaven were collapsing and earth falling, and the peaks were shaking and the mountains crumbling — all were greatly startled. Just as they were thinking to send and ask, the bells jingled, the horse came to the central camp, and Yunchang, holding up Hua Xiong's head, threw it on the ground; the wine was still warm. A later poet wrote a poem in his praise, saying: 'Awe rocks heaven and earth — the first merit of all; / At the camp gate, the painted drums roll their boom-boom. / Yunchang, halting his cup, plies his heroic valour — / While the wine still warm, he beheads Hua Xiong.'
paragraphs.rhyme:
[Cao](char-cao-cao) bade pour out a cup of wine, well-warm'd,
And gave to [Guan Yu](char-guan-yu) ere he was forth-arm'd.
Said [Guan Yu](char-guan-yu): 'Pour the wine; set it aside,
I shall return.' Out of the tent his stride;
He took his blade, and leapt upon his steed.
The lords without the pass heard drums proceed
With roaring sound; the cries rose loud and far,
As though the heavens crash'd, the mountains jarred.
All started, all alarm'd. Ere they could send
To ask, the harness-bells came near the tent;
A horse rode in. [Guan Yu](char-guan-yu), in upraised hand,
Held [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong)'s head; cast it before the band,
The wine yet warm. A later poet sung
These lines in praise, that on his deed are hung:
'His might shakes heaven-earth — the foremost feat!
At camp-gate, painted drums in boom-boom beat.
[Guan Yu](char-guan-yu) halts the cup, his valour shown,
Ere wine grew cold, [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong)'s head lay prone.'

paragraphs.original: 曹操大喜。只見玄德背後轉出張飛，高聲大叫：「俺哥哥斬了華雄，不就這裏殺入關去，活拏董卓，更待何時！」袁術大怒，喝曰：「俺大臣尚自謙讓，量一縣令手下小卒，安敢在此耀武揚威！都與趕出帳去！」曹操曰：「得功者賞，何計貴賤乎？」袁術曰：「既然公等只重一縣令，我當告退。」操曰：「豈可因一言而誤大事耶？」命公孫瓚且帶玄德、關、張回寨。眾官皆散。曹操暗使人齎牛酒撫慰三人。卻說華雄手下敗軍，報上關來。李肅慌忙寫告急文書，申聞董卓。卓急聚李儒、呂布等商議。儒曰：「今失了上將華雄，賊勢浩大。袁紹為盟主，紹叔袁隗，現為太傅；倘或裏應外合，深為不便，可先除之。請丞相親領大軍，分撥剿捕。」
paragraphs.prose: Cao Cao was greatly pleased. Just then, from behind Xuande, Zhang Fei stepped out and shouted with a great voice, 'My elder brother has cut off Hua Xiong's head — why do we not now press through the pass and seize Dong Zhuo alive? What more do we wait for?' Yuan Shu, in great wrath, shouted, 'Even our great ministers are humble; how dare a small soldier under a mere County Magistrate flaunt himself here in display of might? Drive them all out of the tent!' Cao Cao said, 'Reward those who do merit — what calculations of high or low?' Yuan Shu said, 'Since you all only honour a County Magistrate, I shall withdraw.' Cao said, 'Can the great affair be ruined by a single word?' He ordered Gongsun Zan to take Xuande, Guan, and Zhang back to camp for now. The officers all dispersed. Cao secretly sent men with cattle and wine to comfort the three. Now to tell of the defeated soldiers under Hua Xiong, who reported up to the pass. Li Su hastily wrote an urgent dispatch and sent it to Dong Zhuo. Zhuo at once gathered Li Ru, Lü Bu, and others to take counsel. Ru said, 'Now we have lost our superior general Hua Xiong, and the rebels' force grows great. Yuan Shao is the alliance chief, and Shao's uncle Yuan Wei is now Grand Tutor; if there should be coordination from within and without, it would be most ill for us — we should remove him first. I beg the Chancellor to lead the great army in person, dividing the forces to suppress them.'
paragraphs.rhyme:
[Cao Cao](char-cao-cao) joyful. From behind [Liu Bei](char-liu-bei) sprang
[Zhang Fei](char-zhang-fei) forth, with thunder-cry that rang:
'My brother slew [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong)! Why press not through
The pass, take [Dong Zhuo](char-dong-zhuo) alive? What waiting do?'
[Yuan Shu](char-yuan-shu) in great wrath cried: 'Our great lords yield
With modesty; yet one from country-field,
A small foot-soldier 'neath a magistrate,
Dares flaunt his might before our council's gate!
Drive all of them from out the tent away!'
[Cao](char-cao-cao): 'Reward by merit — high or low, why weigh?'
[Shu](char-yuan-shu): 'If ye prize thus a magistrate's small man,
I take my leave.' [Cao](char-cao-cao): 'Shall one word's mere span
Wreck our great cause?' He bade [Gongsun Zan](char-gongsun-zan) lead
[Liu Bei](char-liu-bei), [Guan Yu](char-guan-yu), [Zhang Fei](char-zhang-fei) back, with steady speed.
The lords dispers'd. [Cao](char-cao-cao) sent in stealth a hand
With beef and wine, to soothe that brother-band.
Now [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong)'s defeated soldiers came in dread
Up to the pass. [Li Su](char-li-su) wrote dispatch sped
Urgent to [Dong Zhuo](char-dong-zhuo); Zhuo summon'd straight
[Li Ru](char-li-ru), [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu), and others, to debate.
Ru spake: 'Now [Hua Xiong](char-hua-xiong), our chief, is slain;
The rebels' force is wide in their domain.
[Yuan Shao](char-yuan-shao) heads their league; while within our court square,
[Yuan Wei](char-yuan-wei), his uncle, holds Grand Tutor's chair.
Should they within-without conspire, 'twere ill;
First strike the uncle. Then, my lord, fulfill,
Yourself the great host now in person command;
Divide the forces; crush the rebel band.'

paragraphs.original: 卓然其說，喚李催，郭汜，領兵五百，圍住太傅袁隗家，不分老幼，盡皆誅絕，先將袁隗首級去關前號令。卓遂起兵二十萬，分為兩路而來：一路先令李催，郭汜，引兵五萬，把住汜水關，不要廝殺；卓自將十五萬，同李儒，呂布，樊稠，張濟，等守虎牢關。這關離洛陽五十里。軍馬到關，卓令呂布領三萬大軍，去關前紮住大寨。卓自在關上屯住。
paragraphs.prose: Zhuo agreed with his words, and called Li Jue and Guo Si, who led five hundred soldiers and surrounded the house of the Grand Tutor Yuan Wei, slaying all without distinction of young or old; first they took Yuan Wei's head to display before the pass. Zhuo then raised two hundred thousand troops, divided into two roads: along one road he sent Li Jue and Guo Si first, with fifty thousand troops, to hold Sishui Pass and not to engage; Zhuo himself, with one hundred and fifty thousand, together with Li Ru, Lü Bu, Fan Chou, Zhang Ji, and others, held Hulao Pass. This pass is fifty li from Luoyang. When the troops arrived at the pass, Zhuo bid Lü Bu lead thirty thousand of the great army to make camp before the pass. Zhuo himself encamped upon the pass.
paragraphs.rhyme:
Zhuo gave assent. He call'd up [Li Jue](char-li-jue), [Guo Si](char-guo-si),
And bade them lead five hundred troops to seize
[Yuan Wei](char-yuan-wei)'s Grand Tutor house. None there were spar'd,
All young and old were slain. [Wei](char-yuan-wei)'s head, declar'd
A warning, was display'd before the pass.
Zhuo rais'd two hundred thousand troops, en masse,
And split the host in two: one part assign'd
To [Li Jue](char-li-jue), [Guo Si](char-guo-si) — fifty thousand bind
Up [Sishui Pass](loc-sishui-pass), but not to fight. The rest,
Fifteen myriads — Zhuo himself address'd,
With [Li Ru](char-li-ru), [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu), [Fan Chou](char-fan-chou), [Zhang Ji](char-zhang-ji), and more,
Held [Hulao Pass](loc-hulao-pass), full fifty li before
[Luoyang](loc-luoyang). When troops arriv'd, [Zhuo](char-dong-zhuo) bid
[Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) with thirty thousand strong amid
The plain to camp. Zhuo on the pass-top stay'd,
Encamp'd above, his lordly station made.

paragraphs.original: 流星馬探聽得，報入袁紹大寨裏來。紹聚眾商議。操曰：「董卓屯兵虎牢，截俺諸侯中路，今可勒兵一半迎敵。」紹乃分王匡，喬瑁，鮑信，袁遺，孔融，張楊，陶謙，公孫瓚，八路諸侯，往虎牢關迎敵。操引軍往來救應。八路諸侯，各自起兵。河內太守王匡，引兵先到。呂布帶鐵騎三千，飛奔來迎。王匡將軍馬列成陣勢，勒馬門旗下看時，見呂布出陣：頭戴三叉束髮紫金冠，體挂西川紅錦百花袍，身披獸面吞頭連環鎧，腰繫勒甲玲瓏獅蠻帶；弓箭隨身，手持畫戟；坐下嘶風赤兔馬；果然是人中呂布，馬中赤兔！
paragraphs.prose: An express scout heard of it, and brought report into Yuan Shao's main camp. Shao gathered his men for council. Cao said, 'Dong Zhuo encamps at Hulao and cuts off our middle road; we should now lead half our forces to engage him.' Shao then divided eight lords — Wang Kuang, Qiao Mao, Bao Xin, Yuan Yi, Kong Rong, Zhang Yang, Tao Qian, Gongsun Zan — to go to Hulao Pass to engage. Cao led troops to and fro to support them. The eight lords each set forth. The Grand Administrator of Henei, Wang Kuang, arrived first. Lü Bu, with three thousand iron cavalry, came flying out to meet him. Wang Kuang arrayed his troops in battle line, and reining his horse beneath the gate-flag, looked out — and saw Lü Bu come forth: upon his head, a three-pronged hair-binding crown of purple gold; upon his body, a hundred-flower battle-robe of West Sichuan red brocade; clad in linked-ring armour with beast-faced swallow-head; at his waist, a tightening-armour ornate lion-barbarian belt; with bow and arrows on his person, painted halberd in his hand, and beneath him the neighing Red Hare horse — truly, 'Among men, Lü Bu; among horses, Red Hare!'
paragraphs.rhyme:
An express scout brought word; with flying speed
He reach'd [Yuan Shao](char-yuan-shao)'s main camp. [Shao](char-yuan-shao) call'd in heed
The lords for council. [Cao](char-cao-cao) said: '[Dong Zhuo](char-dong-zhuo) lies
At [Hulao Pass](loc-hulao-pass), our middle road denies.
Half-troops should ride to meet.' [Shao](char-yuan-shao) parcell'd eight:
[Wang Kuang](char-wang-kuang), [Qiao Mao](char-qiao-mao), [Bao Xin](char-bao-xin), Yuan Yi, straight,
[Kong Rong](char-kong-rong), [Zhang Yang](char-zhang-yang), [Tao Qian](char-tao-qian), [Gongsun Zan](char-gongsun-zan) — all
To [Hulao Pass](loc-hulao-pass) to fight beyond the wall.
[Cao](char-cao-cao) led his troops in to-and-fro support.
The eight lords each set forth in their own sort.
[Wang Kuang](char-wang-kuang), Grand Administrator of Henei,
Arriv'd the first. [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu), in array
Of three thousand iron horse, came flying down.
[Wang Kuang](char-wang-kuang) array'd his men; beneath the crown
Of gate-flag, on his horse, look'd out, and there
[Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) emerg'd: upon his head, the fair
Three-prong'd, purple-gold, hair-binding crown;
On body, hundred-flower brocade-red gown
Of West Sichuan; beast-mask'd, swallow-headed mail
Of linked-rings clad him; at his waist did trail
The lion-barbarian belt of tighten'd grace;
Bow-arrows on him; painted halberd's brace
In hand; beneath, the Red Hare neigh'd to wind.
Truly, 'mid men, [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) — no peer to find;
'Mid horses, Red Hare — none of equal kind.

paragraphs.original: 王匡回頭問曰：「誰敢出戰？」後面一將，縱馬挺鎗而出。匡視之，乃河內名將方悅。兩馬相交，無五合，被呂布一戟刺於馬下，挺戟直衝過來。匡軍大敗，四散奔走。布東西衝殺，如入無人之境。幸得喬瑁、袁遺兩軍皆至，來救王匡，呂布方退。三路諸侯，各折了些人馬，退三十里下寨。隨後五路軍馬都至，一處商議，言呂布英雄，無人可敵。
paragraphs.prose: Wang Kuang turned and asked, 'Who dares go forth to fight?' From behind, a general spurred his horse forth with spear levelled. Kuang looked: it was Fang Yue, a famed general of Henei. The two horses crossed; in less than five rounds, Lü Bu pierced him with one halberd-thrust, and he fell dead from his horse. Halberd in hand, Lü Bu rushed straight on. Kuang's army was utterly defeated, and scattered in all directions. Bu charged east and west, as though entering a place without men. Luckily Qiao Mao and Yuan Yi's two armies arrived to rescue Wang Kuang, and Lü Bu retreated. The three lords' forces had each lost some men and horses; they retreated thirty li and made camp. Soon the five other armies arrived, and they took counsel together, saying that Lü Bu's heroism was such that none could match him.
paragraphs.rhyme:
[Wang Kuang](char-wang-kuang) turn'd: 'Who dares to fight?' From rear
A general sprang on horse, with lance held clear,
Fang Yue, of Henei fam'd. Two horses cross'd;
In less than five rounds, [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu)'s halberd toss'd
Through Fang Yue's body; dead, he fell from horse.
[Lü Bu](char-lu-bu), halberd thrust, charg'd in his course.
[Wang Kuang](char-wang-kuang)'s force was rout'd; men on every side
Fled scatter'd. [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) east-and-west could ride
Like one within a land of vacant men.
[Qiao Mao](char-qiao-mao) and Yuan Yi hurried to defend
With both their hosts; [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) then drew back.
The three lords' hosts had losses on their track;
They fell back thirty li, encamp'd that day.
Soon five more hosts arriv'd; in due array,
They held close counsel: '[Lü Bu](char-lu-bu)'s heroism great,
No man can match him; none can stand his weight.'

paragraphs.original: 正慮間，小校報來：「呂布搦戰。」八路諸侯，一齊上馬．軍分八隊，布在高岡。遙望呂布一簇軍馬，繡旗招颭，先來衝陣。上黨太守張楊部將穆順，出馬挺鎗迎戰，被呂布手起一戟，刺於馬下。眾大驚。北海太守孔融部將武安國，使鐵鎚飛馬而出。呂布揮戟拍馬來迎。戰到十餘合，一戟砍斷安國手腕，棄鎚於地而走。八路軍兵齊出，救了武安國。呂布退回去了。眾諸侯回寨商議。曹操曰：「呂布英勇無敵，可會十八路諸侯，共議良策。若擒了呂布，董卓易誅耳。」
paragraphs.prose: Just as they were considering, a scout came in to report, 'Lü Bu is challenging battle.' The eight lords mounted at once, the army divided into eight columns, set upon the high ridge. They saw afar a cluster of Lü Bu's cavalry, embroidered banners waving, charging first. The Grand Administrator of Shangdang, Zhang Yang's general Mu Shun rode out with levelled spear to engage; Lü Bu, with one rise of his halberd, pierced him from his horse. All were greatly shocked. The Grand Administrator of Beihai, Kong Rong's general Wu Anguo, with iron mace, came flying out on horseback. Lü Bu wielded his halberd and slapped his horse to meet him. After ten and more rounds, with one halberd-stroke he severed Wu Anguo's wrist; Wu cast down his mace and fled. The eight armies all rushed forth and rescued Wu Anguo. Lü Bu retreated. The lords returned to camp for council. Cao Cao said, 'Lü Bu's heroism is matchless — let us call together the eighteen lords and consult upon a good plan. If we could capture Lü Bu, Dong Zhuo would be easy to slay.'
paragraphs.rhyme:
A scout came in: '[Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) doth challenge straight!'
The eight lords mounted swift, marshall'd their state;
Eight columns rang'd along the ridge they stood.
[Lü Bu](char-lu-bu)'s array appear'd; embroider'd, woo'd
The wind their banners — first they came to charge.
Mu Shun, of [Zhang Yang](char-zhang-yang)'s Shangdang host so large,
Rode forth with level'd spear to fight [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu);
But [Bu](char-lu-bu)'s one halberd-stroke pierc'd Mu right through,
He fell from horse, slain. All grew pale, aghast.
Then Wu Anguo, of [Kong Rong](char-kong-rong)'s troop, came fast
On horse with iron mace, [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) to face.
[Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) wav'd halberd, slapp'd his steed apace.
Ten rounds and more, the halberd's mighty stroke
Sever'd Wu's wrist; the mace he dropp'd; he broke
To flee. Eight armies sallied as relief
And sav'd Wu Anguo; [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) drew back in brief.
The lords return'd to camp, took counsel still.
[Cao](char-cao-cao) said: '[Lü Bu](char-lu-bu)'s prowess hath no equal will.
Let eighteen lords convene, devise good plan;
If [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) caught, [Dong Zhuo](char-dong-zhuo) is easy man.'

paragraphs.original: 正議間，呂布復引兵搦戰。八路諸侯齊出。公孫瓚揮槊親戰呂布。戰不數合，瓚敗走。呂布縱赤兔馬趕來。那馬日行千里，飛走如風。看看趕上，布舉畫戟望瓚後心便刺。旁邊一將，圓睜環眼，倒豎虎鬚，挺丈八蛇矛，飛馬大叫：「三姓家奴休走！燕人張飛在此！」
paragraphs.prose: Just as they were taking counsel, Lü Bu again led his troops in challenge. The eight lords went forth together. Gongsun Zan, brandishing his lance, fought Lü Bu in person. After only a few rounds, Zan was defeated and fled. Lü Bu let his Red Hare gallop in pursuit. That horse travelled a thousand li in a day, and flew like wind. As he was about to overtake him, Bu lifted his painted halberd and aimed at Zan's back to thrust. From the side, a general — round-glaring eyes, tiger-whiskers bristling upright — wielding a zhang-eight serpent-spear, came galloping forth and shouted, 'Slave of three surnames, halt! Zhang Fei, the Yan-man, is here!'
paragraphs.rhyme:
While they yet plann'd, [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) again the call
Of challenge gave; the eight lords sallied all.
[Gongsun Zan](char-gongsun-zan) wav'd lance, in person fought [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu);
But few rounds pass'd, [Zan](char-gongsun-zan) was defeated through,
And fled. [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) on Red Hare gave him chase,
That horse a thousand li a day in pace
Could fly like wind. As [Zan](char-gongsun-zan) was overta'en,
[Bu](char-lu-bu) rais'd his painted halberd, aim'd amain
At Zan's back-heart. From side, a general flew,
Round-eyes glaring, tiger-whiskers up-grew
And bristl'd stiff; a zhang-eight serpent-spear
He held; on flying horse, he cried out clear:
'Three-surnam'd slave, halt! Yan-man [Zhang Fei](char-zhang-fei)'s here!'

paragraphs.original: 呂布見了，棄了公孫瓚，便戰張飛。飛抖擻精神，酣戰呂布。連鬥五十餘合，不分勝負。雲長見了，把馬一拍，舞八十二斤青龍偃月刀，來夾攻呂布。三匹馬丁字兒廝殺。戰到三十合，戰不倒呂布。劉玄德掣雙股劍，驟黃鬃馬，刺斜裏也來助戰。
paragraphs.prose: Lü Bu, seeing him, abandoned Gongsun Zan and turned to fight Zhang Fei. Fei, rousing all his spirit, fought Lü Bu with full vigour. After fifty and more rounds, neither could prevail. Yunchang, seeing it, slapped his horse and brandished his eighty-two jin Green Dragon Crescent Blade, and came to attack Lü Bu jointly. The three horses fought in a T-shape. After thirty rounds, they could not bring down Lü Bu. Liu Xuande then drew his pair of swords, galloped his Yellow-Mane horse, and charged in from the flank to help.
paragraphs.rhyme:
[Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) saw, left [Zan](char-gongsun-zan), and turn'd to face
[Zhang Fei](char-zhang-fei). Fei rous'd his spirit, fought in pace
Of vigour. Fifty rounds and more they tried;
No winner from the contest could decide.
[Guan Yu](char-guan-yu) saw, and slapp'd his steed, drew nigh
With eighty-two jin Green Dragon, in his eye
The Crescent Moon-blade rais'd; came in to flank.
The three on horseback fought, T-shap'd in rank.
At thirty rounds — [Lü Bu](char-lu-bu) yet stood unbow'd.
[Liu Bei](char-liu-bei) then drew his pair of swords, and proud
Spurr'd Yellow-Mane; he charg'd from flank to side,
And aided in the fight, with sword-strokes wide.

paragraphs.original: 這三個圍住呂布，轉燈兒般廝殺。八路人馬，都看得呆了。呂布架隔遮攔不定，看著玄德面上，虛刺一戟，玄德急閃。呂布蕩開陣角，倒拖畫戟，飛馬便回。三個那裏肯捨，拍馬趕來。八路軍兵，喊聲大震，一齊掩殺。呂布軍馬，望關上奔走；玄德、關、張隨後趕來。古人曾有篇言語，單道著玄德、關、張三戰呂布：漢朝天數當桓靈，炎炎紅日將西傾。奸臣董卓廢少帝，劉協懦弱魂夢驚。曹操傳檄告天下，諸侯奮怒皆興兵。議立袁紹作盟主，誓扶王室定太平。溫侯呂布世無比，雄才四海誇英偉。護軀銀鎧砌龍鱗，束髮金冠簪雉尾。參差寶帶獸平吞，錯落錦袍飛鳳起。龍駒跳踏起天風，畫戟熒煌射秋水。出關搦戰誰敢當？諸侯膽裂心惶惶。踴出燕人張翼德，手持蛇矛丈八鎗。虎鬚倒豎翻金線，環眼圓睜起電光。酣戰未能分勝敗，陣前惱起關雲長。青龍寶刀燦霜雪，鸚鵡戰袍飛蛺蝶。馬蹄到處鬼神嚎，目前一怒應流血。梟雄玄德掣雙鋒，抖擻天威施勇烈。三人圍繞戰多時，遮攔架隔無休歇。喊聲震動天地翻，殺氣迷漫牛斗寒。呂布力窮尋走路，遙望山塞拍馬還。倒拖畫桿方天戟，亂散銷金五彩旛。頓斷絨　走赤兔，翻身飛上虎牢關。三人直趕呂布到關下，看見關上西風飄動青羅傘蓋。張飛大叫：「此必董卓！追呂布有甚強處！不如先拿董賊，便是斬草除根！」拍馬上關，來擒董卓。正是：擒賊定須擒賊首，奇功端的待奇人。未知勝負如何，且聽下文分解。
paragraphs.prose: The three of them encircled Lü Bu, fighting as if upon a revolving lantern. The eight armies all stared in dumbstruck wonder. Lü Bu could not parry or block; looking toward Xuande's face, he made a feigned thrust with his halberd, and Xuande quickly dodged. Lü Bu then opened out a corner of the line, dragged his halberd low, and galloped his horse back. The three would not let him off, and slapped their horses to give chase. The eight armies, with shouts loud as thunder, rushed forth to overwhelm. Lü Bu's force fled toward the pass; Xuande, Guan, and Zhang followed in pursuit. There was an ancient piece of verse, written solely upon Xuande, Guan, and Zhang fighting Lü Bu: 'The destiny of the Han came to its turn under Huan and Ling; the blazing red sun was sinking in the west. The traitor minister Dong Zhuo deposed the Junior Emperor; Liu Xie, weak and timorous, was startled in his very dreams. Cao Cao sent forth his proclamation to the realm; the lords, in righteous wrath, all raised their armies. They met to set up Yuan Shao as alliance chief, and swore to uphold the royal house and bring forth great peace. Marquis Wen Lü Bu was beyond compare in the world; his heroic gifts were boasted abroad in the four seas. His silver scale-armour, set in dragon-scales, shielded his form; on his hair-binding cap of gold, a pheasant-tail plume was set. The studded jewelled belt, with beast-faces engraved in deep relief, and the patterned brocade robe, with phoenixes flying, shone bright. His dragon-steed, leaping, raised the very wind of heaven; his painted halberd, gleaming, flashed like autumn waters. As he came out to challenge — who dared meet him? The lords' livers split, their hearts grew cold. Out leapt Yide, the Yan-man Zhang Fei, holding his serpent-spear of zhang-eight length. His tiger-whiskers, bristling upright, tossed like golden threads; his round eyes, glaring wide, struck out with lightning's flash. They fought to the heat, yet could not part the day; before the line, Yunchang himself was stirred to wrath. His Green Dragon precious blade gleamed like frost and snow; his battle-robe of parrot-figure flew with butterflies. Wherever the horse-hooves trod, ghosts and spirits wailed; before his face, a single rage drew streams of blood. The hero-lord Xuande drew forth his pair of swords, rousing the awe of heaven and showing his fierce valour. The three encircled and fought a long while; with parrying and blocking, there was no rest. Their shouts shook heaven and earth in their fall; the slaughter-air filled all, and Ox and Dipper grew cold. Lü Bu, his strength spent, sought a road to flee; gazing afar at the mountain pass, he slapped his horse and turned. Dragging his painted-shaft Sky-Square halberd low, he scattered his five-colour brocade gold-thread pennants; he snapped his harness-cord and let fly Red Hare, leaping up into the saddle, soaring up to Hulao Pass.' The three pursued Lü Bu straight to the foot of the pass, and saw upon the pass, in the west wind, a green silken canopy fluttering. Zhang Fei cried in a great voice, 'This must surely be Dong Zhuo! What virtue is there in chasing Lü Bu? Better first to seize Dong the traitor — that is cutting up the grass and pulling out the root!' He slapped his horse and rode up to the pass to seize Dong Zhuo. Truly: 'To seize the rebels, you must first seize the chief of rebels; / strange merit is reserved indeed for strange men.' We do not know the outcome — listen to the next chapter for the answer.
